text:
marco: Heads-up — canary run on dedicated-qa shows a tail-latency regression for mixed prefill+decode traffic. Not huge, but consistent on ~8k token prefill + streaming decode cases.
lia: saw similar in prod-like replay yesterday, mainly when requests hit a paged-prefill kernel then fallback to flash decode. KV cache churn looks suspicious.
sam: can you paste the profiler slice?
marco: sure — main snippet from nvprof-like sampling (trimmed):
```
Timeline: decode starts at t=0ms
prefill: paged_attention_kernel (avg 14ms) x 60
decode: flash_attention_smallbatch (avg 9ms) x 240
KV memcpy: 7.2ms spikes during kernel switch
kernel_switch: 2.1ms overhead per request
cpu->gpu queueing: occasional 3-10ms jitter
```

marco: hypothesis: kernel crossover causes extra KV page materialization + memcpy when decode path expects contiguous KV layout. Paging wins for large prefill but penalizes small-batch decode due to copy-on-use.
anita: that's in line with what I saw — when sequence length distribution is bimodal (long prefill then short decode), the runtime picks paged kernels for prefill threshold heuristics. But decode microbatches are small and prefer fused/flash path. The migration isn't zero-cost.
sam: any perf bot alerts? perf-bot: Perf Canary Alert: dedicated-qa/canary-17: +13% p99 latency for chat workload between 1765530000 and 1765550000. Suspected area: attention kernel routing.
lia: I ran a narrow A/B: force-flash for everything vs allow-paged. Results: flash-everywhere reduces p99 on mixed workload by ~8% but increases GPU memory usage ~6% and hurts big-prefill throughput (10% drop).
marco: so there's a tradeoff. We need a smarter runtime heuristic to pick kernels based on end-to-end request shape, not per-phase. Ideas: 1) lookahead: if request is prefill+decode (chat) prefer a decode-friendly KV layout; 2) keep copy-on-read for paged but pre-allocate contiguous KV for hot sessions; 3) dynamic probe: small probe to measure memcpy cost.
anita: +1 for lookahead. We can detect chat sessions by presence of streaming flag + prefill token count. Might also use a soft TTL on KV pages to avoid immediate compaction.
sam: what about continuous batching interplay? If we delay a bit to batch decode microrequests we could amortize kernel_switch overhead. But that risks latency SLOs. How much batching headroom do we have?
marco: measured microbatch sizes: median decode batch=2, 95th=6. Continuous batching window is 6-8ms currently; increasing to 12ms doubled batch size but added median latency +4ms. For tail, it helped.
lia: propose experiment matrix: (A) early-flash-for-chat, (B) paged-for-prefill-only with prefetch-to-contig on decode, (C) slightly-larger batch window for decode-only requests. Run each on canary for 2h with replay.
anita: I'll add flags and lightweight metrics: kernel_choice (paged|flash|fused), kv_memcpy_time_ms, kernel_switch_count, decode_microbatch_size. Need to surface in console per-model route.
sam: also add a perf regression guard: if p99 rises >7% then rollback. devops-bot: Canary deployment 17 -> patch/kernel-crossover-expts started (id: canary-17-kkc).
marco: quick note — profiler trace shows memcpy hotspots at same address offsets when page->contig happens. Might be fixable by changing page allocator alignment or a one-shot move to pinned memory earlier in prefill.
lia: could we do a hybrid kernel that accepts paged backing but implements flash-like attention when decode small? That seems like a lot of kernel engineering. Short-term runtime heuristics are better.
anita: agreed. I'll implement the flags and metrics tonight. Who can run the A/B and gather traces?
sam: I can schedule the replay runs and collect perf traces + nvtx markers. Also will add a microbench with 8k prefill + 1-8 decode tokens, varying batch windows.
marco: thanks. Capture a CSV with columns: scenario, kernel_policy, mean_latency_ms, p99_ms, gpu_mem_mb, memcpy_ms_avg, decode_batch_median — that'll make comparing easy.
perf-bot: Note: please annotate runs with model and quantization level. Different quant/ops change kernel perf a lot.
lia: good call. We'll run on g5x instances and also a quantized 4bit variant.
anita: I'll push a dashboard tile in Console: kernel routing heatmap + kv memcpy histogram.
marco: ok let's reconvene after 2x2 runs. If heuristic shows >6% p99 improvement without >8% mem bump, we'll roll to prod canary.
sam: 👍 scheduling now. ETA: results by EOD tomorrow.
devops-bot: Canary deployment updated: canary-17-kkc -> running experiment flavor A/B/C.
marco: Thanks everyone. Short-term goal: eliminate the copy-on-switch tail. Long-term: consider unified kernel path.
lia: filing a follow-up doc with microbench results + kernel threshold proposal. Link when ready. :rocket:
